ORDER IN FIRST APPEALS 1.

Present appeals are preferred under section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short "the Act") read with section 96 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (for short "the Code") by the State against the common judgment and award dated 27.4.2022 passed by the learned Principal Senior Civil Judge, Arvalli @ Modasa in Land Acquisition Reference Case Nos. 39 of 2021 & 40 of 2021 and 42 of 2021 to 44 of 2021, whereby, total amount of Rs.2139/- per sq mtr for the acquired lands has been awarded with other consequential benefits to the original claimants.

entities.text: Land Acquisition Reference Case Nos. 39 of 2021 & 40 of 2021 and 42 of 2021 to 44 of 2021
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
2. The lands of the claimants situated at village Bajkot, Tal:
Modasa, Dist: Sabarkantha came to be acquired by the State for the purpose of construction of four land Highway road from Shamlaji to Halol by issuing notifications under sections 4 and 6 of the Act on 25.1.2008 and 20.8.2008 respectively.
The Special Land Acquisition Officer vide his award dated 29.5.2010 awarded Rs.7.50/- per sq mtr as compensation for the acquired lands.

The claimants preferred reference under section 18 of the Act before the Court of learned Principal Senior Civil Judge, Arvalli @ Modasa, who by impugned common judgment and award, partly allowed the reference of the original claimants and granted total amount of compensation of Rs. 2139/- per sq.mtr inclusive of compensation awarded by the Special Land Acquisition NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4482/2024 ORDER DATED: 07/04/2026 undefined Officer.

entities.text: Principal Senior Civil Judge, Arvalli @ Modasa
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Feeling aggrieved by the award, the State has preferred the present appeals.

3. On perusal of the impugned award, more particularly, para 14.2 and 19 thereof, it appears that the learned Reference Court relied upon the judgment of LAQ Case No.34/2007/2010 (Land Acquisition Reference Case Nos.4 of 2017 and 5 of 2017),
wherein, the learned Reference Court has fixed the market value of the acquired land at Rs.2139/-
per sq mtr. Para 14.2 and 19 reads as under:-
"14.2 Both the petitioners have further stated in their affidavits that there is a system established by the Hon'ble Government for determining the prices of land by the The State Of Gujarat vs Patel Laddhabhai Harjibhai on 7 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76487364/
2 Special Land Acquisition Officer.

entities.text: Land Acquisition Reference Case Nos.4 of 2017 and 5 of 2017
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

entities.text: State Of Gujarat vs Patel Laddhabhai Harjibhai
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: According to that system, the market price is determined by a committee headed by the Collector after consulting and deliberating with the Deputy Planner and on that basis the market price of the land is determined.

Accordingly, it has been stated that no action has been taken by the Hon'ble Government to determine the market price of their land and the true price of the lands acquired by the petitioners has not been determined.

Further, the said petitioners have stated in their testimonies that the boundary of Bajkot village starts from Saira Chowkdi by placing a bridge over Mazum river and immediately after that the acquired lands of the petitioners are located, stating that the boundaries of Saira and Bajkot villages are adjacent to each other, stating that the lands acquired in Saira lands under the judgment given under Land Reference No. 145/2010 to 147/2010 are only 200 meters away from the lands acquired in the present work and further,
regarding the lands acquired by the petitioners under the present work, the award dated 29.5.2010 issued by the Special Land Acquisition Officer by this court in LAQ Case No. 34/2007/2010, the court references NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4482/2024 ORDER DATED: 07/04/2026 undefined made by the applicants of other acquired lands, Land Reference No. 4/2017 and 5/2017, have been given a judgment on the merits by this court on 16.4.2021, considering the evidence adduced in those cases, in which the market value of the agricultural land acquired by the other applicants of this award in the year 2008 has been fixed at Rs. 2139/- per sq.m.
and in that circumstance, the acquired lands of the applicants of the present work and the acquired lands of the applicants of Land Reference No. 4/2017 and 5/2017 have been fixed at Rs. 2139/- per sq.m.
The lands are from the same award and as per the judgment dated 16.4.2021 dated Land Reference No. 4/2017 and 5/2017, the applicants of the present work are legally entitled to compensation.

In the above judgment, the Hon'ble Court has fixed the value of the agricultural land acquired from this award at Rs. 2139/- per sq.m., and accordingly, it has been submitted that the applicants of the present work should be given compensation.

In the cross- examination of the said applicant, the fact that a notice was given at the time the land was acquired for this work and that they had accepted the compensation has been admitted, but they have clarified that they have accepted the compensation with objections.
Thus, in the cross-examination of the said witness, he has adhered to the facts stated in his affidavit and no fact that would help the affidavit has come on record.

19. In the present case, the agricultural lands of the applicants have been acquired by the Special Land Acquisition Officer vide award L.A.Q. Case No. 34/2007/2010 dated 29.5.2010 and the lands of other applicants have also been acquired by the same award.

The owner-occupiers of those acquired lands have submitted reference applications before the Special Land Acquisition Officer stating that the compensation paid for their acquired lands vide award L.A.Q. Case No.
34/2007/2010 dated 29.5.2010 is less than the current market price and thereafter the said reference applications were referred to the Hon'ble Court.

The reference applications of the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4482/2024 ORDER DATED:

3 07/04/2026 undefined applicant vide Land Reference Case No. 4/2017 and Land Reference Case No. 5/2017, on the basis of the evidence presented, a judgment has been given on 16.4.2021 on the merits, in which the market value of the agricultural lands of Moje Bajkot, Ta. Modasa acquired by the said court through the said award has been fixed at Rs. 2139/- per sq.m. in the year 2008.

sentences.text:
Further, the lands acquired in Land Reference Case No. 4/2017 and Land Reference Case No. 5/2017 and the lands acquired by the applicants of the present work, both the lands are acquired for the same purpose on the same day, in the same award L.A.Q. Case No. 34/2007/2010 and the agricultural lands acquired under the said award, in the judgment of Land Reference Case No. 4/2017 and Land Reference Case No. 5/2017, the market value of the acquired lands in the year 2008 has been determined and no appeal has been filed by the respondents against that judgment and in that circumstance the lands acquired in the present case have also been acquired by the award of L.A.Q. Case No.
34/2007/2010, the present applicants are also entitled to get the market value of their acquired agricultural lands as per the judgment of Land Reference Case No.
4/2017 and Land Reference Case No. 5/2017 as per the market value of 1 sq.m. Rs.
2139/- as on the date of notification of Section-4 of the present case.

Therefore, the market value of the land of the applicant which the Acquisition Officer has determined and ordered to pay compensation is not correct and reasonable, as discussed above, in the present case one sq.m. of the acquired agricultural land of the applicant is Rs.
It is decided to pay compensation accordingly by determining the market value of Rs. 2139/-."

4. During the course of hearing, learned advocate Mr.Kashyap Jani placed on record letter dated 18.4.2022, which is taken on record, whereby, it is intimated that the State has accepted the award passed in LAQ Case No.34/2007/2010 (Land Acquisition Reference Case Nos.4 of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4482/2024 ORDER DATED: 07/04/2026 undefined 2017 and 5 of 2017).

Meaning thereby, the award passed in LAQ Case No.34/2007/2010 (Land Acquisition Reference Case Nos.4 of 2017 and 5 of 2017) has become final between the parties and therefore, no reason remains with the State to ventilate a grievance against the impugned common judgment and award on the principle of estoppel.

entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: 5. Moreover, during the course of hearing, learned advocate Mr. Jani places on record Division Bench judgment rendered in case of First Appeal Nos.2210 of 2022 and allied matters, wherein the State has challenged the award of the Special Land Acquisition Officer passed for the land acquired for village Gajan in Land Acquisition Reference Case Nos.4 of 2017 and 5 of 2017 and the Division Bench has granted compensation at Rs.2139/- per sq mtr.

entities.text: Land Acquisition Reference Case Nos.4 of 2017 and 5 of 2017
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
Para 28 of said order reads as under:-
"28.

So far as other set of appeals of village Gajan are concerned, we could notice that the acquisition pertains to same Godhra State highway project, wherein section 4 notification was issued on 14.12.2007 and 26.03.2010.
Again, the reference court has placed reliance upon judgment and award passed in LAR no. 14 to 147 of 2010, while determining the market value of lands so acquired.

The reference court, upon evaluation of material evidence has also noted the peculiar factors and upon due The State Of Gujarat vs Patel Laddhabhai Harjibhai on 7 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76487364/
4 consideration has determined the market value.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Ld. Advocate for the claimants has placed reliance upon award passed by the reference court in the case of LAR no. 4 and 5 of 2017 in the case of lands of village: Bajkot which are situated at a distance of 200 mrts from village Sayara and LAR no. 1 and 2 of 2017 in the case of lands acquired of village: Gajan, which are situated one kms.
From village Gajan.

The NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4482/2024 ORDER DATED: 07/04/2026 undefined reference court has determined market value in aforesaid cases at the rate of Rs.
2139/- per sq.mrts.
For agriculture land.

Additionally, reliance is also placed on award passed by reference court in the case of LAR. No. 96 of 2017 of village: Sayara,
which is an adjoining village wherein the market value is determined at the rate of Rs. 2781 /- sq.mrts for N.A. land and Rs. 2139 / sq.mrts.
For agriculture land.

For the reasons stated in paras 26 & 27 and paras 27 & 28 of the impugned judgement and award, we could notice that the base exemplar relied upon by the reference court is the award passed in reference case no. 145 to 147 of 2010.

Thus, for reasons stated we find no error being committed by the reference court while determining the market value in the lands so acquired in the case of village: Gajan, which is adjoining to village Sayara."
5.1
Learned AGP is unable to point out as to whether order passed by the Division Bench in First Appeal Nos.2210 of 2022 and allied matters is challenged before higher forum or not.
5.2 Thus, the issue remains no more res integra and hence, no ground is made out to interfere with the impugned common judgment and award of the learned Reference Court.
Under the circumstances, present first appeals deserve to be dismissed and are accordingly dismissed.

6. In view of dismissal of both the first appeals, civil applications, if any, do not survive and the same stand disposed of accordingly.
7. Registry to maintain copy of this order in each matter.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4482/2024 ORDER DATED: 07/04/2026 undefined 8. Registry is directed to return back the R & P, if any, to the concerned Court forthwith.

9. The learned Reference Court is directed to disburse the amount of compensation deposited by the State Government after deducting Court fee to the claimants after due verification and identification along with interest and after verifying their right to claim the compensation.
